counting.method_note: tokens = characters / a per-format divisor (see counting.ratios); estimates, not counts. Characters are the measured unit.

compact_text.provenance: v1.5.0 design-pass measurement over the compact pipe cards emitted by discovery/serialize.py. Denser than schema text, hence the lower divisor - the whole reason a flat divisor is wrong.

json_data.provenance: Borrowed from json_schema; no measurement exists for dense numeric JSON. Float-heavy JSON plausibly tokenizes worse (fewer chars per token), so the token figures on result-side payloads are best read as a floor.

json_schema.provenance: v1.5.0 design-pass measurement over this server's own tools/list payload (JSON Schema text: short ASCII keys, punctuation and prose descriptions). Not re-derived here - re-derive with --tokenizer anthropic.

text.provenance: Borrowed from json_schema, whose text is mostly prose descriptions; no measurement exists for the server's plain-English instructions alone.

rejected_methods.flat_chars_per_token: One divisor for every format mis-states every cross-format comparison in this report - the schema-text and compact-text divisors differ by 27%. Within a format it would cancel; the comparisons here are between formats.
rejected_methods.tiktoken: A real tokenizer, but OpenAI's: it undercounts Claude tokens by ~15-20% on prose and more on code/JSON, so it would reintroduce the same class of error. Not wired in on purpose.
